message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"3","text":"But otherwise—not even if he is my child or brother or friend, or is ever related to me by family in some other way, if indeed he is unworthy—not to pass them on for this person’s sake, since it was not proper. I will not fear a plot, nor will I be cajoled by gifts. But even if at some point the books of the proclamations given to me should seem to me not to be true, not even in that case will I pass them on; instead, I will return them. When traveling, I will carry with me whichever of them I happen to possess. But if I do not wish to carry them around with me, I will not allow them to remain at my house; instead, I will entrust them to my bishop, who holds the same faith and proceeds from the same starting points. And if I should happen to fall ill and suspect that I may die, if I am childless, I will do likewise. But even if I die while I have a child who is unworthy or not yet capable, I will do likewise, for I will entrust them to my bishop, so that if the child, on reaching maturity, should happen to be worthy of trust, the bishop will return them to the child as a paternal deposit, in accordance with the wording of the solemn attestation.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἄλλως δὲ οὐδ’ ἂν τέκνον ἢ ἀδελφὸς ἢ φίλος ἢ ἄλλως πως ποτὲ γένους μοι ἀνήκων, ἐάνπερ ἀνάξιος ᾖ, τοῦδε μὴ μεταδοῦναι χάριν, ὡς οὐ προσῆκεν.","chosen":"But otherwise—not even if he is my child or brother or friend, or is ever related to me by family in some other way, if indeed he is unworthy—not to pass them on for this person’s sake, since it was not proper.","rationale":"The main rendering follows a defensible unchanged-text analysis without pretending that it is unique. It takes ἄν conditionally with an understood copula governing the coordinated nominative descriptions; ἐάνπερ ἀνάξιος ᾖ further qualifies the prospective recipient. It takes τοῦδε as a masculine personal genitive governed by the postpositive χάριν across μὴ μεταδοῦναι, while μή negates the infinitive. The preceding books supply the unexpressed object of μεταδοῦναι. The English deliberately retains the anacoluthic infinitive “not to pass” and does not insert an unwritten governing verb such as “I promise” or “I will.” The scalar οὐδέ and the infinitival μή jointly express the emphatic refusal rather than canceling one another."},{"source_quote":"ἄλλως πως ποτὲ γένους μοι ἀνήκων","chosen":"is ever related to me by family in some other way","rationale":"γένους is retained as specifying the sphere of family or kinship, while μοι marks the relationship to the speaker. The precise idiom is unusual, but the family relationship is contextually defensible without changing the genitive to a dative."},{"source_quote":"οὔτε ἐπιβουλὴν φοβηθήσομαι, οὐ δώροις κολακευθήσομαι","chosen":"I will not fear a plot, nor will I be cajoled by gifts","rationale":"ἐπιβουλή denotes a hostile design or plot. “Cajoled” preserves the flattering or persuasive force of κολακεύω without replacing the printed “gifts” with the more interpretive “bribes.”"},{"source_quote":"τὰ διδόμενά μοι τῶν κηρυγμάτων βιβλία μὴ ἀληθῆ εἶναι","chosen":"the books of the proclamations given to me should seem to me not to be true","rationale":"The negation remains within what the books might seem to be; it is not recast as a claim that the books actually are false."},{"source_quote":"ἀποδημῶν δὲ σὺν ἐμοὶ αὐτὰ κομίσω, ἅπερ ἂν τύχω κεκτημένος","chosen":"When traveling, I will carry with me whichever of them I happen to possess","rationale":"ἀποδημῶν describes travel or absence from home, while τύχω κεκτημένος indicates whichever books the speaker happens to have in his possession."},{"source_quote":"εἰ δὲ μὴ βουληθῶ μεθ’ ἑαυτοῦ αὐτὰ περιφέρειν","chosen":"But if I do not wish to carry them around with me","rationale":"The reflexive ἑαυτοῦ is understood as referring contextually to the first-person speaker. The translation does not emend it to ἐμαυτοῦ."},{"source_quote":"τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ μου τῷ τὴν αὐτὴν ἔχοντι πίστιν καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν αὐτῶν ὁρμωμένῳ παρακαταθήσομαι","chosen":"I will entrust them to my bishop, who holds the same faith and proceeds from the same starting points","rationale":"παρακαταθήσομαι describes placing the books with the bishop as a deposit or trust. “Proceeds from the same starting points” retains the metaphor in ἀπὸ τῶν αὐτῶν ὁρμωμένῳ rather than replacing it with an unexplained doctrinal conclusion."},{"source_quote":"τὸν θάνατον ὑποπτεύσαι","chosen":"suspect that I may die","rationale":"This preserves the apprehensive or uncertain force of ὑποπτεύω rather than presenting death as a settled expectation."},{"source_quote":"ἄξιος εἶναι τῆς πίστεως","chosen":"be worthy of trust","rationale":"The immediate context concerns whether entrusted books may safely be returned to the child, so πίστις is taken in the fiduciary sense “trust.” “Worthy of the faith,” referring to the shared religious faith mentioned earlier, remains a viable alternative."},{"source_quote":"ἵνα εἰ μὲν τύχοι, ἐφ’ ἡλικίας γενόμενος, ἄξιος εἶναι τῆς πίστεως, ὡς πατρῴαν παρακαταθήκην τῷ τέκνῳ ἀποδώσει","chosen":"so that if the child, on reaching maturity, should happen to be worthy of trust, the bishop will return them to the child as a paternal deposit","rationale":"The child is the contextual subject of τύχοι, γενόμενος, and εἶναι, whereas the bishop who holds the deposit is the contextual subject of ἀποδώσει. πατρῴαν παρακαταθήκην preserves the legal image of a deposit originating with the child’s father. The unpaired μέν and the shift of implicit subject are treated as anacoluthic features rather than silently rewritten."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ τὸν τῆς διαμαρτυρίας λόγον","chosen":"in accordance with the wording of the solemn attestation","rationale":"διαμαρτυρία refers to the formal attestation introduced in the preceding sections, while λόγος here denotes its stated wording or terms."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἄλλως δὲ οὐδ’ ἂν τέκνον ἢ ἀδελφὸς ἢ φίλος ἢ ἄλλως πως ποτὲ γένους μοι ἀνήκων, ἐάνπερ ἀνάξιος ᾖ, τοῦδε μὴ μεταδοῦναι χάριν, ὡς οὐ προσῆκεν.","issue":"The verified printed sentence is syntactically anacoluthic and does not express a finite governor for μεταδοῦναι. The main translation adopts the strongest contextual allocation: conditional ἄν with an understood copula, personal τοῦδε governed discontinuously by χάριν, and μή negating an infinitival resumption of the preceding undertaking. It therefore preserves an English infinitival fragment rather than inventing a finite predicate. A material alternative takes οὐδέ with an omitted finite refusal and regards μὴ μεταδοῦναι as its restatement, but that requires more unexpressed structure. A neuter partitive τοῦδε, “some of this,” is also grammatically possible, but it leaves the force and attachment of χάριν substantially less secure. No change to τοῦδε, either negation, or the printed word division is proposed. The chosen analysis is contextual and defensible, though not uniquely established; this is ordinary syntactic ambiguity rather than an unreadable source or an invented restoration.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"εἰ δὲ μὴ βουληθῶ μεθ’ ἑαυτοῦ αὐτὰ περιφέρειν","issue":"The third-person reflexive form ἑαυτοῦ refers contextually to the first-person speaker of βουληθῶ. This is an unusual reflexive alignment but does not require an emendation or prevent a defensible translation.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"παρακαταθήσομαι·,","issue":"The selected edition prints a middle dot immediately followed by a comma. This is an editorial punctuation anomaly and does not affect the lexical text or the construction.","proposed_reading":"παρακαταθήσομαι,","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἵνα εἰ μὲν τύχοι, ἐφ’ ἡλικίας γενόμενος, ἄξιος εἶναι τῆς πίστεως, ὡς πατρῴαν παρακαταθήκην τῷ τέκνῳ ἀποδώσει","issue":"The clause has an unpaired μέν and an implicit subject shift: the child is the natural subject of reaching maturity and being worthy, while the bishop is the natural subject of returning the deposit. The custody context supports this reading, but “worthy of the faith” remains a viable lexical alternative to “worthy of trust.” These are ordinary anacoluthic and referential ambiguities, not grounds for restoring omitted text.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
